title: Recall Quiz: The Elizabethan Age & Christopher Marlowe

questions.q: Who among the following is generally NOT considered one of the 'University Wits'?
questions.explanation: Ben Jonson belongs to the later Jacobean era and was not part of the University Wits.

questions.q: The phrase 'Marlowe's mighty line' was coined by:
questions.explanation: Ben Jonson used this phrase in his tribute to Shakespeare to praise Marlowe's powerful use of blank verse.

questions.q: In which play does the protagonist sell his soul to the devil in exchange for 24 years of absolute knowledge?
questions.explanation: Doctor Faustus is Marlowe's tragic masterpiece about a scholar's pact with the devil.
Blank verse consists of unrhymed lines in iambic pentameter, heavily popularized by Marlowe.

questions.q: The Elizabethan age coincided with which major cultural movement spreading through Europe?
questions.explanation: The Renaissance, with its focus on humanism, deeply influenced Elizabethan literature.

questions.q: Which play by Marlowe heavily influenced Shakespeare's 'The Merchant of Venice'?
questions.explanation: Marlowe's character Barabas in The Jew of Malta is a clear precursor to Shakespeare's Shylock.

questions.q: Which of the following playwrights is grouped with the University Wits despite not having attended a university?
questions.explanation: Thomas Kyd, author of The Spanish Tragedy, is grouped with them due to his style and association, despite lacking a university degree.

questions.q: Marlowe's tragic heroes are typically characterized by:
questions.explanation: Marlovian heroes like Faustus and Tamburlaine are driven by an overwhelming lust for power, knowledge, or wealth.
